rgb: The camera wearer stands behind an L-shaped wooden checkout counter inside a shop, facing a person in a dark blue jacket standing across the counter roughly 3.8 to 4.2 metres in front and out of reach. On the front counter far out of arm's reach (about 3.8 to 4.4 metres away) are a black cash register to the lower right, a flat promotional sign in the lower centre, and a red plastic shopping basket to the lower left, while a brown paper bag sits on the side counter section to the right about 3.7 to 4.0 metres away, and a glass pastry display case stands behind the person to the upper left at roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres. In frame 1, the person leans backward and reaches their left hand across the counter to touch the cash register keypad while their head is cropped above the top edge of the frame and the counter occludes everyone's lower bodies below the waist. Across frames 2 and 3, the person steps forward slightly to stand upright facing away from the camera wearer, resting their left hand on the counter edge in frame 3 while extending their right arm toward the red basket on the left, with their head still mostly out of view above the frame in frames 1 through 4. In frame 4, the camera wearer pans slightly left as the person turns their torso rightward toward the side counter and lifts the red basket rightward, leaving the basket mostly cropped out on the right edge. By frame 5, the red basket sits on the right side counter directly in front of the brown paper bag about 4.0 metres from the camera wearer, and the person stands to the left of the side counter with their head and glasses now visible, facing right toward the basket and looking downward rather than at the camera wearer.
depth: The depth map shows an L-shaped checkout counter extending through the distant field (4.4–4.7 m, brightest white) to about 3.5–3.8 m on the right, with a standing person across the counter at roughly 3.8–4.2 m in front of the camera wearer and a pastry display case at 0.6–1.2 m on the left. On the counter far out of arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the other person are a register keypad at the bottom-right (4.4–4.6 m), a red plastic shopping basket at the bottom-left in frames 1–3 (4.3–4.6 m) that is moved onto the right counter wing (3.8–4.0 m) in front of a upright brown paper bag (3.6–3.9 m) by frame 5, and counter jars on the far right (4.2–4.5 m). Across the 5 frames, the person faces away from the counter and camera wearer while leaning backward in frame 1 so their left arm reaches 4.5 m at the keypad, stepping slightly forward to ~3.8–4.0 m in frames 2–3 while reaching their right hand to the basket at the left edge, turning slightly right toward the bag in frame 4 (~4.1 m), and standing upright at ~3.9–4.1 m facing away and slightly right in frame 5 with their lower body occluded by the counter Throughout. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the continuous distance gradient along the L-shaped counter surfaces, the recessed gap behind the counter where the person stands, and the step in depth between the red basket and the paper bag behind it in frame 5. However, the map is unreliable around the open lattice holes of the red basket in frame 2 (which bleed background depth), softens the keypad and jar contours into indistinct blobs, and clips the background hallway and doorway within 1.5 m to uniform black.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the standing person in front of the counter (roughly 3.8–4.2 m from the camera wearer and out of reach) as a pink mask across all 5 frames, while labeling the register keypad at the bottom-right (4.4–4.6 m, out of arm's reach) as 'laptop' in frame 1 and 'keyboard' in frame 3, and the elevated glass display case on the left (0.6–1.2 m, ~3.0–5.0 m to the person's right) as 'tv' in frames 2 and 4. Across the sequence, the person's mask shifts from leaning right with an extended left arm overlapping the top edge of the register mask in frame 1, to standing centrally with the head cropped by the top frame boundary in frames 2–4 and the right arm extending to the left frame edge in frame 3, to occupying the left side of the frame in frame 5 as they turn slightly toward the right counter. The masks capture how the counter edge occludes the person's lower torso and legs from below in every frame, while the top image border cuts off the person's head in frames 1–4 before their head and glasses re-enter the frame in frame 5 looking downward toward the counter rather than directly at the camera wearer. Compared to motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frame 1), segmentation provides sharp outer boundaries for the person's torso and reaching arm relative to the register surface. However, it is highly unreliable for scene completeness and classification: it completely misses the L-shaped counter, the red basket, and the brown paper bag, drops the register in frames 2, 4, and 5 and the display case in frames 1, 3, and 5, misclassifies the register and display case as 'laptop'/'keyboard' and 'tv', and leaves hollow black holes inside the person's jacket and white shirt in frames 2 and 4.
pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing only a magenta left hand at the bottom-right in frame 1 (~4.5 m from the camera wearer) and far from the center-right counter in frame 3 (~4.2 m), alongside yellow upper-body skeletons for the person in frames 2 and 5 (~3.8–4.1 m away and out of reach) and a mislocalized yellow cluster on the left in frame 4. In frames 2 and 5, the shoulder, hip, and facial keypoints show the person standing behind the counter facing generally away from the camera wearer and angled slightly to the right, with their head tilted downward toward the counter surface rather than looking into the lens, and their lower body below the hips occluded by the counter. In frame 1, the magenta finger keypoints explicitly trace the person's left hand flat against the register keypad far out of arm's reach of both people, while in frame 2 the yellow arm segments show the left arm hanging down far from the counter gap and the right arm bent far from the red basket, and in frame 3 the magenta hand keypoints mark the left fist resting on the counter surface. Even when the person's dark jacket sleeves blend into the dark background or suffer motion blur in RGB, the pose map pinpoints exact joint articulations, finger orientations on the keypad, and head/eye landmarks in frames 2 and 5. However, the pose map is spatially unreliable across much of the strip: it misses the entire body skeleton in frames 1 and 3, fails to detect the person's right arm reaching for the basket in frame 3, misses the hands in frames 2, 4, and 5, and hallucinates a sideways yellow body skeleton on the glass pastry case (~0.8 m away on the left) in frame 4 while missing the actual person standing at the center-right.
